mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to increased borrowing costs and reduced corporate earnings, which results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within two months signals an improving labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 1% month-over-month signals increased consumer demand, which boosts corporate revenues and earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where RSAFS increases by more than 1%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 0.5% month-over-month signals a contraction in supply, which can lead to increased prices and reduced corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month, it signals a tight labor market with strong job growth, boosting consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increase > 200,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) increase by more than 5% month-over-month and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) remains stable (change < 0.1%), it signals strong demand without significant inflationary pressure, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increase > 5% in 1 month and CPIAUCSL change < 0.1%
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 1% over six months signals a strong tightening cycle, leading to reduced liquidity and increased borrowing costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) grows by more than 2% quarter-over-quarter and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.3% in the same period, it signals strong economic growth and improving labor conditions, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increase > 2% QoQ and UNRATE decrease > 0.3% in 3 months
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, the hypothesis is rejected.
